spec.name: Blueprint Spitfire Mk V
spec.description: A Supermarine Spitfire fighter built as a living cyanotype blueprint: deep Prussian-blue surfaces traced with pale-cyan panel lines, glowing cyan roundels and bright technical linework on every part.
spec.layout: A low-wing single-seat fighter standing on its undercarriage, level on the floor: main wheels at z≈2.35 and a small tailwheel at z≈-4.35 touch y=0; everything else hangs above the floor. From front to back: a pointed brass-capped spinner with three wide propeller blades (tips banded in glowing cyan) at z≈4.1-4.9, then the rounded engine cowling with cooling gills and exhaust stubs (z 2.55-4.1), the elliptical monocoque fuselage with a flat spine deck under the bubble canopy (z -3.45 to 2.55), then the tapered rear fuselage into the tall swept fin (top y 3.45) and horizontal tailplanes (z -3.45 to -4.95). The elliptical wings span x ±5.6 at y≈1.5, root chord about 3 m tapering to 1.1 m at the rounded tips, with a slight dihedral. The style shows on every part: all main surfaces wear the deep Prussian blue of blueprint paper; every seam, panel line, rivet row, control-surface edge and stencil is a separate thin part in pale cyan or bright cyan, so the whole plane reads as a technical drawing made solid; roundels, walkway trim and the gun-sight glow provide the only strong accents (white, red, brass, glowing cyan).

parts.builds: Engine section and propeller. Cowling: a lofted tube from the firewall mount (z 2.55, radius ~0.62, slightly taller than wide) tapering to radius 0.42 at the spinner base (z 4.1), wearing paper blue; a row of ~10 vertical cooling-gill slats on each side between z 2.9 and 3.6, each slat a thin paperShade plate with a pale line-colour edge strip; two small raised access panels on the cowling top in panel blue with line-colour outlines. Exhaust stubs: three short faired stacks per side at z 2.8-3.4, x ±0.62, steelDark with a line-colour rim on each outlet. Spinner: a lathe cone from z 4.1 (r 0.42) to z 4.78 (r 0.07) in paper blue with a brass hub cap and a thin glow-colour ring where cowling meets spinner. Propeller: three blades on propHub, each a tapered, slightly twisted blade 0.95 long from the hub, paperShade with a line-colour leading-edge strip and the outer 0.12 banded in glow cyan; a thin glowing cyan arc ring of radius 0.95 at z 4.2 traces the prop disc like a blueprint annotation. Add thin line-colour panel-seam strips around the cowling at two frame stations.
parts.attaches: Cowling back face meets the fuselage at the firewall mount (z 2.55); spinner and blades ride the propHub joint at [0, 2.05, 4.15].

parts.builds: Monocoque hull. A loft along z from the firewall (z 2.55) back to the tailRoot mount (z -3.45): elliptical sections ~0.62 wide at the firewall, widest (~0.66) at the cockpit z≈1.0, tapering to ~0.30 at the tail, centreline y ~1.8-2.0 with a rounded belly; flat-ish spine deck at y 2.15 from the cockpit back (the deckTop mount plane), wearing paper blue with two or three large subtle panel-tone patches in panel blue inset on the flanks. Blueprint linework: thin line-colour frame-station strips wrapping the hull at 7-8 stations, two longitudinal stringer lines each side, and a spine ridge strip on the deck; a few tiny ink-colour vent and filler dots. Markings: RAF roundels on both flanks at z≈0.3, y≈1.85 — concentric flat discs (roundelBlue r 0.22, white r 0.15, red r 0.07) each with a hairline ink rim, seated slightly proud of the skin. A small steel antenna mast on the deck just behind the cockpit with a short ink antenna wire stub running back. Underside: two small ink-colour breather scoops under the belly near the wing root.
parts.attaches: Front face closes onto the nose at the firewall mount; rear face closes onto the tail at the tailRoot mount; top deck carries the cockpit at the deckTop mount; wing roots bury into the flanks at the wingRoot mounts.

parts.builds: Elliptical cantilever wings, mirrored left and right about x=0. Each wing runs from the root (x ±0.6, buried into the fuselage flanks at the wingRoot mounts) to a rounded tip at x ±5.6; root chord ~3.0 m (z 0.5-3.1 at the root, narrowing to ~1.1 m at the tip), thickness ~13% of chord at the root, a slight dihedral lifting the tip ~0.25 m. Build each as a loft of airfoil sections along the span, paper blue on top and bottom, with panel-blue panel patches on the upper surface, ink-colour rib lines running chordwise every ~0.5 m out to mid-span, a line-colour spanwise spar strip, and a row of tiny line-colour rivet dots along the root. Armament: two Hispano cannon per wing whose steel barrels (r 0.045, length 0.55) protrude forward from the leading edge at x ±1.7 and ±2.6, each with a brass muzzle ring and a tiny glow-colour muzzle cap; gun ports as small ink-colour oval plates on the wing top above each barrel. Markings: upper-surface roundels at x ±2.4, z≈2.3 (roundelBlue r 0.30, white r 0.20, red r 0.09, ink rim), a trim-colour walkway strip along the inboard leading edge, and a small glow-colour landing light set flush in the leading edge near the root (x ±1.2). A thin steel pitot tube under the left wing tip leading edge, 0.35 long with a glow tip.
parts.attaches: Roots bury into the fuselage flanks at the wingRootL and wingRootR mounts, sharing the fuselage box at z 0.5-3.1; undersides at x ±1.05, y 1.3, z 2.5 carry the gearMounts.

parts.builds: Empennage. Fin: a swept curved fin from the tailRoot mount deck (z -3.45) up to y 3.45, built as an extruded slab ~0.09 thick with a rounded leading edge, paper blue with a line-colour outline strip around its edges; the fin flash near the top leading edge — three vertical stripes (roundelBlue, white, roundelBlue) each ~0.10 wide, seated flat on the fin. Rudder: the rear half of the fin from the rudderHinge line (z -4.45) aft, a thinner slab with a small horn balance at its bottom, panel blue with a line-colour edge, riding the rudderHinge joint, plus a small trim tab at its base. Tailplanes: two horizontal slabs spanning x ±1.9 from the rear fuselage, chord ~0.9 tapering to a rounded tip, slight dihedral, paper blue with ink-colour edge lines. Elevators: the outboard rear halves riding elevatorL and elevatorR, panel blue with a line-colour edge and a small horn balance each. A tiny glow-colour tail lamp at the very tip of the fin, and three thin line-colour frame-station strips wrapping the fin.
parts.attaches: Front faces close onto the fuselage rear at the tailRoot mount (z -3.45); control surfaces ride the rudderHinge, elevatorL and elevatorR joints.

parts.builds: Canopy and cockpit furniture sitting on the deckTop mount plane (y 2.15). Canopy framing: a windscreen frame of thin steel arcs at z≈0.5 with a flat framed glass pane in glass colour, then two hoop frames at z≈0.95 and z≈1.35, all steel, with glass-colour panes between, the bubble roof peaking at y 2.65 and fairing down to the deck at z≈1.75; a line-colour seam strip follows the canopy base rail. Interior hints (readable through the side panes): a seat-colour seat slab with an ink-colour frame rail at z 0.9-1.2, and a small headrest fairing. Ahead of the windscreen: a dark ink-colour instrument panel cowl at z≈0.45 with four tiny line-colour dial discs and hairline ink needles, and a reflector gun sight on a steel stalk at z≈0.55, y≈2.45 — a small brass-colour body with a glowing cyan sight dot. Thin steel canopy side rails run along the deck at x ±0.5 from z 0.4 to 1.7.
parts.attaches: Base sits on the fuselage spine deck at the deckTop mount (y 2.15, z 0.15-1.8), fully inside the fuselage box footprint.

parts.builds: Undercarriage — the only part touching the floor. Main gear, mirrored: a raked main leg from each gearMount (x ±1.05, y 1.3, z 2.5) down-forward to the wheel hub (x ±1.15, y 0.33, z 2.35), built as a two-piece steel strut — a thick main leg with an ink-colour seam strip and a smaller rear drag strut joining mid-leg to the fuselage belly; a small steel torque-link detail beside each leg. Wheels ride the wheelFL and wheelFR joints: radius 0.33, width 0.14, ink-colour rubber tire with a thin paperShade sidewall ring, and a steel hub disc carrying five small ink-colour holes arranged in a ring and a line-colour rim. Tailwheel: a steel fork from the tailWheelMount (y 0.55, z -4.3) down to a small wheel at the tailWheel joint — radius 0.16 at y 0.16, z -4.35, ink-colour tire with a steel hub. Both main wheels and the tailwheel rest exactly on y = 0.
parts.attaches: Leg tops meet the wing undersides at the gearMountL and gearMountR mounts; the fork meets the rear fuselage underside at the tailWheelMount; wheels ride the wheelFL, wheelFR and tailWheel joints.

Thinking Process:

1.  **Analyze the Request:** The goal is to create a single TypeScript module for a complex, stylized model (a Spitfire fighter plane) using the `agentic-3js-builder` SDK. The style must be "cyanotype blueprint," low-poly, highly detailed in structure/form but simple in shading (flat colors), and adhere to strict model constraints (180-340 parts, 700-1100 lines, etc.).

2.  **Analyze the Subject (Spitfire):**
    *   Subject: Spitfire Fighter Plane.
    *   Style: Cyanotype blueprint (suggest color palette: blue/cyan/white, cross-section lines, technical drawing aesthetic).
    *   Composition: Large, streamlined, complex geometry, wings, engine cowling, cockpit.
    *   Scaling: Real-world size (need reasonable proportions). A modern Spitfire is large.

3.  **Determine Model Structure & Scaling:**
    *   A full Spitfire is complex. I need to divide it into 3-6 logical parts.
    *   Let's aim for 4 parts: Fuselage/Cockpit, Wings/Canards, Engine/Propeller, Landing Gear.
    *   Dimensions (Estimate for a medium-sized, stylized version): Length ~12-15m, Height ~4-5m.
    *   Center on X=0, Y=0 (ground/platform), faces +Z.

4.  **Define Palette (Cyanotype Blueprint):**
    *   `hull`/Body: Deep blueprint blue (e.g., `#000080` or a slightly lighter technical blue).
    *   `detail`/Lines: Cyan/Light blue (e.g., `#00FFFF`).
    *   `accents`/Cockpit/Metal: White or a pale grey/cyan.
    *   Let's use:
        *   `blueprintBlue`: `#001F3F` (Dark, classic blueprint)
        *   `cyanLine`: `#00FFFF` (Bright cyan for outlines and technical details)
        *   `panelGrey`: `#A0A0A0` (For metal/panel lines)
        *   `cockpitYellow`: `#FFD700` (Classic cockpit framing/instrument highlight)

5.  **Define Joints/Skeleton (Crucial for a plane):**
    *   A plane doesn't have a skeleton, but the components (wings, flaps, gear) move relative to the fuselage. I need joints to allow for articulation, even if static.
    *   `root` (Fuselage)
    *   `wingRoot` (Attached to fuselage)
    *   `flapsL`, `flapsR` (Joint on wing)
    *   `gearFrontL`, `gearFrontR` (Hinge on landing gear)

6.  **Detailed Part Construction Plan (Iterative Refinement):**

    *   **Part 1: Fuselage and Cockpit (The Core)**
        *   Shape: Long cylinder/wedge.
        *   Details: Canopy structure, intakes, gun placement.
        *   Primary structure: Use `b.chain` or simple large primitives.
        *   *Focus: Defining the core geometry.*

    *   **Part 2: Wings (Main Lifting Surfaces)**
        *   Shape: Long, tapered swept wings.
        *   Details: Leading edges, rivets (small parts), internal structure representation (ribs/struts built as small cyan lines).
        *   Need to attach to `body` via `b.stick` onto a surface point.

    *   **Part 3: Engine & Propeller (Nose)**
        *   Shape: Cylindrical cowling, spinner.
        *   Details: Propeller blades (thin, multi-pronged shapes), exhaust ports.
        *   Attached to the front of the fuselage.

    *   **Part 4: Undercarriage (Landing Gear)**
        *   Shape: Strong struts, spoked wheels (simplified).
        *   Details: Hinge points, shock absorption cylinders.
        *   Attached to specific points under the fuselage via defined joints.

7.  **Writing the Code (Self-Correction/Refinement during drafting):**
    *   *Constraint Check:* Use primitives. Keep it stylized/blocky. Cyanotype look means heavy reliance on outlines (`cyanLine`) and flat bases (`blueprintBlue`).
    *   *Modeling Technique:* Instead of aiming for hyper-realism, I must emphasize the *blueprint* look. Every surface detail (panel lines, rivets) must be a separate, small cyan primitive on the body part.
    *   *Implementation:* Use `b.chain` for the main body shape, then use `b.surface` and `b.stick` to add cockpit frames, inlets, and surface details.

8.  **Final Polish (Adherence to Craft/Art Direction):** Ensure the colors are applied spatially (e.g., wing undersurface detail vs. top surface color). Ensure the skeleton is defined correctly first.

**(Self-Correction on Complexity):** A full Spitfire is huge for 340 parts. I will make it large and robust, leaning into the blocky, primitive nature while maintaining the aerodynamic silhouette. The blueprint aesthetic allows for simplification of texture into geometric representation (e.g., using lines and hatches instead of complex meshes).

A Spitfire is roughly 6-7 meters long, 3-3.5 meters wide, and 2 meters high (including canopy).

**D. Empennage**
*   The twin tail surfaces. Needs to align with the back of the mid-fuselage.

**E. LandingGear**
*   Needs defined joints/mount points for connection to the main body.

---

**Size:** X=4.0 (width), Y=2.5 (height), Z=7.0 (length).
**Palette:**
*   `hull`: `#050022` (Deep navy for blueprint lines)

**Joint:**
*   `body` (root)

**Mounts:**
*   Need wing attachment points (Should be near the mid-section). Let's say `wingRoot1` and `wingRoot2` on the mid-fuselage.
